index.features.title: Why is Keeply more than a backup tool?
index.features.subtitle: Backup tools only remember the current file; Keeply remembers every version, every note, every decision you made. Six months later when a client asks "who decided this?" you open Keeply and find the answer in seconds — that's a capability backup tools simply cannot give you.
index.features.1.title: Remember your WHY
index.features.1.desc: Don't just remember what changed — remember why you changed it.
index.features.1.detail: Six months later when a client asks "Who made this decision?" you won't need to dig through emails. Open Keeply — the answer is right there.
index.features.2.title: Your project time machine
index.features.2.desc: Every save is like taking a snapshot. Go back to any day, anytime.
index.features.2.detail: Made a mistake? Just go back. Client changed their mind? Find the old version in three seconds. Audit time? Complete records right here.
index.features.3.title: Edit boldly, we remember everything
index.features.3.desc: No more choosing between "make it better" and "too scared to change it."
index.features.3.detail: Keeply protects every version so you can experiment freely. No matter what you change, you can always go back.
index.features.4.title: See every change, side-by-side
index.features.4.desc: Visual diff for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDFs, and images.
index.features.4.detail: Not just a list of modified files — Keeply shows you exactly what changed, with Office documents, PDFs, and images displayed side-by-side with highlighted differences. For every other file type, track versions and restore any point in seconds.
index.features.5.title: Handles big files silently
index.features.5.desc: Blender, PSD, video — all work out of the box.
index.features.5.detail: Keeply automatically detects 38 binary file formats and any file over 10 MB, routing them through large-file storage without a single configuration step. No LFS setup, no repo bloat, no broken saves on large projects.
index.features.6.title: Try bold changes safely
index.features.6.desc: Create a work copy, experiment, then merge back.
index.features.6.detail: Work copies let you branch off from your project to try a radical new design or a risky refactor, then merge the changes back when they're ready — or delete the work copy if the experiment didn't pan out. Your main project stays untouched the whole time.

index.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
index.faq.1.a: Yes. Keeply's version management runs fully locally — no cloud, no account. Your project files, version history, and notes all stay on your hard drive or NAS, and you can work in airplane mode or on an air-gapped machine. By default the app touches the network only for license verification and update checks (which you can disable). The one exception is the optional AI assistant (off by default): if you enable it and select files, that content goes from your machine directly to the AI provider you choose — or use a local model and stay fully offline.
index.faq.2.q: How is Keeply different from Dropbox or Google Drive?
index.faq.2.a: Dropbox and Google Drive sync the current state of files; Keeply records every version as a separate snapshot. Dropbox and Drive charge per user per month; Keeply is free for individuals and will have a flat $25/month Team plan (coming soon) regardless of team size. Your files live on your disk, not a vendor server, so you are not locked into a subscription.
index.faq.3.q: What happens to my files if I stop paying?
index.faq.3.a: Nothing. Keeply files are stored on your hard drive or NAS in a standard folder structure you control. Even if you uninstall Keeply, the files and their version history remain readable by any file manager. You are not paying for access to your own work — the Founding Member license is a one-time perpetual payment, and the free tier stays free forever.
index.faq.4.q: Can my team share files without per-seat licensing?
index.faq.4.a: Yes. In the free tier, teams already share a single vault folder over NAS or a shared drive — Keeply does not count seats. The upcoming Team plan ($25/month flat, planned) adds invite-code onboarding and an admin dashboard, but still without per-seat fees. Compare this with Dropbox Business at $20 per seat per month, which costs $120/month for a 6-person team.
index.faq.5.q: What file types does Keeply support?
index.faq.5.a: Any file. Keeply shows side-by-side visual diff for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, and images. For every other file type — Blender, PSD, video, CAD, 3D models, source code — Keeply tracks versions and lets you restore any point in seconds. Files over 10MB and 38 known binary formats are auto-detected and routed to large-file storage without any setup or LFS configuration.
index.faq.6.a: Keeply currently ships for Windows 10 or later and macOS on Apple Silicon. A Linux build is on the roadmap but has not shipped yet. If Linux support is critical for your workflow, please tell us via the contact form — we prioritize platform support based on actual user demand, and every request is logged.
index.faq.7.q: What is the $599 Founding Member plan?
index.faq.7.a: A one-time payment for a perpetual license, limited to the first 500 buyers. You get current Keeply features forever, plus all Team plan features automatically when the Team plan ships. No recurring billing, no surprise price hikes. For comparison, $25/month for 24 months equals $600 — Founding Member pays for itself in under two years and keeps going.
index.faq.8.q: Why can't I use my ChatGPT Plus / Claude Pro subscription with the AI assistant?
index.faq.8.a: Consumer subscription terms prohibit third-party apps from automating those accounts, and users have been suspended without warning or refund for doing so. Official API keys are the safe way to do this — they are designed for exactly this, and you pay only for what you actually use.
index.faq.9.q: Is my AI API key safe in Keeply?
index.faq.9.a: Your key is stored only in your computer's system credential vault (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain). Keeply never uploads, retains, or even sees it — requests go from your machine directly to the provider you chose.
index.faq.10.q: How much does the AI assistant cost to use?
index.faq.10.a: You pay your AI provider directly, by actual usage — processing a document typically costs a few cents (USD). Keeply never handles the money and adds no markup; your exact bill is in your provider's dashboard. With a local model, there are no API fees at all.
index.faq.11.q: Can I use the AI assistant completely offline?
index.faq.11.a: Yes — in local mode, Keeply works with models running on your own machine (for example Gemma or Llama via Ollama). Your files never leave your computer, and there are no API fees.
privacy.meta.title: Privacy Policy — Keeply
privacy.meta.description: Keeply is a local-first desktop application: version management runs on your computer, and Keeply itself collects no usage data. Learn the minimal data we actually process — and where data goes if you enable the optional AI assistant.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.highlight: Keeply is a local-first desktop application — version management runs entirely on your computer or the locations you choose, and Keeply itself collects no usage data. Your files stay on your device; only if you enable the optional AI assistant and explicitly select files does that content go from your computer directly to the AI provider you choose (see “When you choose to use the AI assistant” below). This privacy policy explains the minimal data we actually process, who handles it, and your rights.

privacy.files.title: By default, your files stay on your device
privacy.files.p1: Keeply manages version history of your project files locally. All project files are stored only on your computer or NAS. Apart from the optional AI assistant described in the next section — which you must enable yourself and which sends only content you explicitly select — Keeply does not upload, transmit, access, read, or process your file contents. We do not operate any cloud storage servers and cannot view your work at any time.
privacy.files.p2: Network communications made by the Keeply desktop application are limited to:
privacy.files.li2: Update checks: Checks whether a new version is available
privacy.files.li3: AI assistant (optional, off by default): only when you connect an AI service and explicitly select content — your computer connects directly to the AI provider you chose (see the next section)
privacy.files.p3: Outside the AI assistant case above (which you enable, and which covers only content you explicitly select), the desktop application does not transmit your file contents or file metadata. Keeply currently sends no usage statistics either (see §2.5).
privacy.ai.title: When you choose to use the AI assistant
privacy.ai.p1: The AI assistant is off by default. Only when you connect an AI service yourself (by entering your own API key) and explicitly choose which files the AI may see is the content of those files sent from your computer directly to the AI provider you selected (for example OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or a local model running on your own machine). This never passes through any Keeply server — Keeply does not handle, store, or see your content.
privacy.ai.p2: If you choose local mode (running an AI model on your own computer, for example with Ollama or LM Studio), your file content never leaves your computer at all — and there are no API fees.
privacy.ai.p3: Your API key is stored only in your computer's operating-system credential vault (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain). Keeply does not upload, host, or see your key; usage and fees are settled directly between you and the AI provider — Keeply never handles the money and adds no markup.
privacy.ai.p4: Once content reaches the AI provider you selected, its retention, deletion, and use for training are governed by that provider's terms and privacy policy (for example the privacy policies of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google) — which provider to use is your decision, and Keeply does not endorse any provider. Please review your provider's policy before sending.
privacy.ai.p5: Keeply's error reporting and statistics never include your file contents or AI conversation content. In addition, every AI edit is first shown to you as a proposal, applied only after you confirm it, fully recorded in version history and labeled as an AI-assistant edit, and reversible with one click.

privacy.license.title: Data processed during license verification
privacy.license.p1: To verify your software license, Keeply communicates with Keygen.sh (Keygen LLC, Virginia, USA). The data transmitted includes:
privacy.license.li1: License key — Confirms whether the license is valid
privacy.license.li2: Vault location identifier — A one-way hash of your project vault's unique ID (cannot be traced back to the original identifier or your file contents)
privacy.license.li3: Application version — Checks compatibility and license scope
privacy.license.li4: Vault location token — A hashed identifier of your team's vault location (cannot be reversed to the actual storage path)
privacy.license.p2: We do not transmit your name, email address, or any file contents. Keygen holds SOC 2 Type II certification, uses Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) for international data transfers, and retains server logs for up to 30 days and analytics data for up to 90 days.
privacy.license.p3: For details, see the Keygen.sh Privacy Policy.
privacy.payment.title: Data processed during payment
privacy.payment.p1: All purchases of Keeply are processed by Paddle.com, which serves as our Merchant of Record. Your transaction is with Paddle, not Keeply. Paddle collects and processes: name, email address, billing address, payment method, location, and IP address.
privacy.payment.p2: Keeply never receives, stores, or accesses your credit card number or full payment details. Paddle may share limited buyer information (name, email, and transaction details) with us solely for order fulfillment and product support.
privacy.payment.p3: For details, see the Paddle Privacy Policy and Paddle Buyer Terms.
privacy.payment.p4: Legal basis (GDPR): Contractual necessity (Article 6(1)(b)) and legitimate interest in fraud prevention (Article 6(1)(f)).
privacy.website.title: Data collected on our website
privacy.website.p1: The Keeply marketing website (keeply.work) detects your preferred language entirely within your browser — we do not send your IP address to any third party for this purpose. Your language choice is saved to your browser's local storage only after you explicitly pick one from the language menu, or open a language-specific link (e.g. keeply.work/de/). (Historical note: before 2026-04-23 the website used a third-party IP geolocation service; see the Keeply governance document for the decision, alternatives considered, and removal timeline.)
privacy.website.p2: If you contact us by email, we retain the correspondence to respond to your inquiry. You will not be added to any marketing list unless you explicitly opt in.
privacy.telemetry.title: Usage statistics
privacy.telemetry.intro: Keeply currently collects no usage statistics and sends none.
privacy.telemetry.current.body: Shipped Keeply builds contain no active usage-statistics reporting. Reporting code exists inside the application, but shipped builds are configured with no reporting endpoint, so the entire pipeline is dormant — nothing is sent, including the install-source count. Keeply's error reporting and statistics never include your file contents or AI conversation content.
privacy.telemetry.future.body: If a future version enables anonymous usage statistics, we will update this privacy policy before that version ships, clearly inform you inside the application, and ask for your consent where applicable.

terms.s3.5.title: 3.4 Definitions
terms.s3.5.p1: "Team Vault" means a shared storage location — including but not limited to a Network Attached Storage (NAS) device, file server, self-hosted Git server, or cloud-hosted Git remote repository — designated as the central collaboration point. A Team Vault is identified by a unique location token generated by the Software and stored within the repository.
terms.s3.5.p2: "Vault Location" means the logical location marker associated with a Team Vault, derived from the repository's embedded location token and/or the normalized remote URL. Vault Locations are classified into the following types:
terms.s3.5.p2a: (a) "Canonical" means the Vault Location designated as the source of truth for team versions; exactly one (1) per Team Vault;
terms.s3.5.p2b: (b) "Shared Mirror" means a Vault Location that is a full snapshot synchronized from the Canonical and shared across the team; at most one (1) per Team Vault;
terms.s3.5.p2c: (c) "Release" means a version snapshot produced from the Canonical at a specific point in time; unlimited in number;
terms.s3.5.p2d: (d) "Clone" means a local working copy derived from the Canonical on a member's device; unlimited in number.
terms.s3.5.p3: The data form of a Vault Location may be selected at creation time: "Standard mode" allows direct browsing and editing of the Canonical via the file explorer, and the Canonical may be modified by any user with access to that folder; "Protected mode" uses a protected repository format, where the Canonical contents may only be modified through the Software interface and destructive history-changing operations are rejected. Both Standard and Protected modes are available on the Free and Team plans. Personal workflows (version history, file diff, Release publishing, unlimited users, etc.) are identical between the two plans; the Team plan's distinguishing features are team governance tools, not increased capacity or additional locations.
terms.s3.6.title: 3.5 Vault Location Rules
terms.s3.6.p1: Changes to a Shared Mirror Location are subject to the following (applicable only to the Team plan):
terms.s3.6.li1: (a) A cool-down period of seven (7) days from the most recent change taking effect (a period during which no further changes may be made);
terms.s3.6.li2: (b) No more than six (6) changes within any rolling 365-day period;
terms.s3.6.li3: (c) Migration of repository data (including the embedded location token) to new storage hardware does not constitute a Shared Mirror Location change, provided the location token remains unchanged.
terms.s3.6.p2: When a Shared Mirror Location has not been accessed for ninety (90) consecutive days, the Software will notify the admin, but will not automatically release the location.
terms.s3.6.p3: Vault Location changes on the Free plan are not subject to cooldowns or annual limits; the foregoing limits apply to the Team plan only.
terms.s3.7.title: 3.6 License Scope
terms.s3.8.title: 3.7 Fair Use
terms.s3.8.p1: Keeply plans are designed for use by a single organization's team. "Organization" means a company or legal entity and its employees, consultants, and contractors. Users shall not: (a) Share license keys or credentials with unauthorized third parties; (b) Artificially circumvent Vault Location limits by routing multiple independent teams through a single storage location; (c) Resell, sublicense, or redistribute access to the Software or any Vault.
terms.s3.8.p2: If we detect usage patterns significantly exceeding expected norms (e.g., team size exceeding 10× the plan average), we may contact you to discuss a more suitable plan. Our goal is to find the right fit, not to penalize growth.

about.meta.description: Keeply is run by one person, Ting-Wei Tsao — built for small teams who share one folder every day. Coding, support, and refunds all go straight to the founder.
about.title: About Keeply
about.intro: Keeply is for small teams that fight over a shared folder every day. If anyone on your team has ever asked "who still has last Thursday’s version?", hunted for "really_final.dwg", or watched a file get overwritten by someone else — this page tells you who built Keeply, why, and how long it’ll be around.
about.s1.title: Why I built a "version control" tool
about.s1.p1: Over the past two years, my company took on a public-works project where one employee was responsible for the CAD construction drawings. His files lived in the company shared folder, where he collaborated with 6-7 other people on the team. When he cleaned up his computer before leaving, he accidentally deleted one of those CAD drawings — and the paper copy of that drawing hadn’t been scanned and filed yet. No file history, no record of changes, no way back to the moment before he deleted it. That one drawing, we had to redraw from scratch.
about.s1.p2: Watching it happen, my first thought wasn’t "our security failed" or "whose fault is this." It was — we’re not stupid. This kind of software was simply never designed to remember who did what. NAS, shared folders, cloud drives — they’re built to let people sync and collaborate, not to let people trace back afterward. I thought: a construction site needs a file-management tool, but not the kind engineers use.
about.s1.p3: I don’t come from a programming background. I lean heavily on AI to write code, and along the way I came across a thing engineers use called git — it remembers "who changed what, and when." That was the moment I realized: engineers have used this capability for decades, but no one had ever brought it onto a construction site. So I started redesigning that capability into a version made for 6-7 non-engineers sharing one set of files. Keeply is that answer.
about.s1.p4: On the site I saw all of these situations — _v3_final.dwg followed by _v3_really_final.dwg, an old/ folder stuffed with 50 past versions, and the team chat asking every few days "who has last Thursday’s drawing?" From then on I kept wondering — what about other small office teams? Designers, lawyers, accounting firms — those places where 6-7 people share one set of files every day, are they doing the same thing? Faking file history by hand with naming conventions and folder structures. The problem isn’t that these teams don’t understand technology; it’s that this technology was never translated for the setting of "people who don’t write code needing to edit one set of files together."
about.s1.p5: Sometimes I wonder whether to build an enterprise edition. So far I haven’t seen concrete demand, and designing blindly without demand only produces something nobody wants. So I’ve chosen to wait — until enough enterprise users come tell me "you should add X," and then I’ll build it properly. When I see that signal, I’ll update this page.
about.s2.title: Keeply’s 5 principles
about.s2.p1.title: Everyone’s own machine is a backup
about.s2.p1.body: You don’t have to trust our servers. Keeply runs on your machine and on every teammate’s machine, and every computer holds a complete file history. A 6-7 person team = 6-7 independent backups. If the shared NAS gets wiped by someone, if Dropbox sync goes wrong, even if the Keeply company disappears tomorrow — you can still pull last Thursday’s version off a colleague’s machine.
about.s2.p2.title: Don’t change the way you already work
about.s2.p2.body: You already have a shared folder, naming habits, and a collaboration flow you trust — none of that needs to change. Keeply doesn’t replace your NAS, doesn’t replace Dropbox, doesn’t replace Google Drive. It keeps file history quietly in the background on each team member’s machine, and you keep working the familiar way. No one has to relearn a tool, no one has to be told "we’re switching to something new."
about.s2.p3.title: Designed for teams that don’t write code
about.s2.p3.body: You and your team open folders, find files, and edit files every day — that’s the most intuitive rhythm of work for most people. Keeply hooks file history into that rhythm: you save a file, and Keeply automatically keeps its history; you want to go back to last Thursday, you just click the timeline. You’ll never see a message like "from now on you have to learn a new tool." If you can open a folder, you can use Keeply.
about.s2.p4.title: Privacy
about.s2.p4.body: Our servers can't see what your team is changing. File history is never uploaded to Keeply, never analyzed by us, never sold. Our only business model is you paying for the Keeply software — not selling your team's data. (If you enable the optional AI assistant, the content you select goes from your machine directly to the AI provider you choose — still never through us.) Once you've paid the license fee, we have nothing to do with your files — what you did in Keeply today simply isn't visible to us.
about.s2.p5.title: Still readable 5 years from now
about.s2.p5.body: Keeply stores file history in open formats, not some closed file we invented. Five years from now, if you want to write your own code to pull it out, move it to the next tool, or copy the whole history backup to another drive — you can do all of that, without asking us, and without our servers needing to be alive. If the Keeply company disappears tomorrow, your file history is still right where it was, and you can open it as usual.
about.s3.title: Who are you handing your files to?
about.s3.p1: Keeply is made by one person. My name is Ting-Wei Tsao. Writing the code, designing the interface, answering support email, processing refunds, replying to your LinkedIn messages — I handle all of it myself. No outsourced support, no PR speaking on my behalf, no marketing team. You write in, and the person who replies is me.
about.s3.p2: I’m a licensed Professional Civil Engineer (I passed Taiwan’s national professional qualification examination), specializing in construction management, and I graduated from the Department of Construction Engineering at National Taiwan University of Science and Technology. For the past two years I’ve worked at a construction company on public-works projects, so the file chaos a site team faces every day is something I’ve lived through.
about.s3.p3: The technical side is the fun part. I lean heavily on AI to write code, and at first I didn’t even know what GitHub was. One time I was overhauling a webapp I was building, AI went on a rampage and broke my stuff, and I wasn’t using git at the time. Luckily AI later reverse-engineered a fix back for me, and only then did I turn around and ask, "how do you solve this kind of thing at the root?" — that was the first time I learned about git.
about.s3.p4: I used to run VPS reselling for customers worldwide, with up to 1,600 customers using my service — so "handing software to strangers over the internet and keeping it running" is nothing new to me. That experience taught me one thing: customers don’t care how big your company is, they care whether you can solve their problem. Keeply being made by one person means there’s no product manager forcing me to add a dashboard, no marketing telling me to write "AI-powered," no support script standing between you and me. Your message comes straight to me. To me, the heart of building a business is helping people solve problems — and what Keeply solves is the daily file chaos that construction sites and small office teams face.
about.s4.title: If Keeply disappears one day, will your data still be there?
about.s4.p1: Short answer: yes. Keeply’s file history lives on your machine and on every one of your teammates’ machines, not on our company’s servers. Even if the Keeply company folds tomorrow, our website goes dark, and the payment system stops — you open Finder (or Windows File Explorer), go into the Keeply folder, and those 200 versions are still right where they were. A team of 6-7 people means 6-7 independent backups.
about.s4.p2: The software license comes with an unconditional 30-day refund. The Team Plan monthly, the Team Plan annual, and the $599 early-access perpetual license all qualify — no reason needed, no form to fill out, just send me one email. See the full terms in the refund policy.
about.s4.p3: And if one day you decide to stop using Keeply and switch to another tool — you can take your data with you. File history is stored in open formats and can be read by third-party software. You won’t be locked into Keeply.
